analysis.title: Brutal
key_insights: SOX is down 10% as of writing. The major trend line has broken, the 200-day MA is far above current levels, and SOX is at its most oversold level since the bull market began. The Market Ear is starting to consider a contrarian dip-buy.

NDX is trading below its range lows and the longer-term trend line, and well below the 200-day MA. Sharp selloffs have been followed by sharp rebounds without a lasting trend. Tech looks tired, especially memory.
VVIX rose 45 points. Nomura's McElligott says an apparent all-clear triggered an aggressive hedge unwind, then the market reversed violently and traders rushed back into protection.

VXSMH is near its yearly highs at about 64, and the options market prices daily moves of roughly 4% in semiconductors. The earlier gap between KOSPI VIX and VXSMH has closed, and The Market Ear says holders of its long semis vol idea should take profits.
Nomura estimates about $61bn of implied vol-control selling after today's shock. These strategies react with a lag, so today's move may feed tomorrow's selling rather than selling today.
Vanda Research says the break below 27,600 could push CTAs outright short. A clean break below 26,800 would likely take CTA exposure toward the Liberation Day lows.

Nomura says discretionary traders are front-running systematic deleveraging, leveraged ETF rebalancing and dealer hedging. Dealers hold about $7bn of negative gamma per 1% SPX move, but the timing of their hedging is uncertain and they may already have sold.
The Market Ear's long Apple anti-AI trade continues to work. Apple is outperforming NDX, and expressing the trade against NVDA is working even better.
Gold is back above the short-term trend line in place since late August but needs to reclaim the 50-day MA ($4,205) for a more persistent move. The 200-day MA sits just below $4,500.

Per Goldman's Quinn, gold saw five straight weeks of speculative selling totalling $19.5B before the squeeze, including $8B in the final week. CTAs were running large gold shorts into the squeeze and have probably covered at least partly.
